module_title: Important Airports and Seaports - Foundational Locations
introduction: Airports and Seaports are crucial infrastructure assets that frequently appear in the 'Geography & Miscellaneous' section of Static GK. In one-day competitive exams like SSC Tier-1 and Railways, the most common questions involve directly matching a famous airport or port with its respective city or state. This level establishes those foundational targets.

core_concepts.title: India's Busiest Airport Hubs
core_concepts.description: Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA) in New Delhi is the busiest airport in India. It is closely followed by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

core_concepts.title: The Gateway of Southern and Eastern India
core_concepts.description: Kempegowda International Airport serves Bengaluru, Karnataka, and is renowned for its rapid expansion. On the eastern side, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport serves Kolkata, West Bengal.

core_concepts.title: India's Premier Major Seaports
core_concepts.description: India has 12 major government-controlled seaports and one corporate port. Mumbai Port is historically the largest natural port, while Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port (formerly Kolkata Port) is the oldest operating major port, unique for being riverine.

important_entities.name: Indira Gandhi International Airport
important_entities.significance: The largest and busiest aviation hub in the country, featuring three functional runways.

important_entities.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport
important_entities.significance: A primary international gateway, famous for handling high passenger density on a constrained layout.

important_entities.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA)
important_entities.significance: Also known as Nhava Sheva. It is the premier container-handling seaport in India.

important_entities.name: Deendayal Port
important_entities.significance: A major hub located in the Gulf of Kutch, consistently leading in terms of absolute cargo volume handled.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Kandla and Kolkata Renaming Traps
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners love to test older versus newer nomenclature. If you see 'Deendayal Port', look for Gujarat (it is the new name for Kandla Port). Similarly, if you see 'Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port', map it to Kolkata, West Bengal.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Shivaji in Mumbai, Netaji in Kolkata
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Directly pair the historic leaders' names with their respective regional airport base: Chhatrapati Shivaji = Mumbai | Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose = Kolkata.

exam_strategy_tips: In Tier-1 exams, focus heavily on the capital cities. Memorize the exact names of airports in tier-1 metro locations as they form the bulk of option matchings.
